text.p: A group of Finns "seeking their inner animal" are learning to behave like chimpanzees on a course marketed as a route to relaxation and better motivation, the daily Helsingin Sanomat said on Monday.

The course in the southern town of Tampere includes learning to sit, move, sound and eat like chimpanzees -- which, contrary to common belief, do not naturally peel their bananas but dig out the flesh of the fruit with their fingers, the paper said.
Aspiring apes also learn to pick each other's "fur" for loose dry skin, which the animals would also eat, the paper said.
